designs.title: How Beer Is Made
designs.why: Clean, confident line work. The three-row grid and arrows read clearly from a distance, and the bold sans headings are well matched. But it has no title, so from 3 m it reads as a textbook infographic, not a garment graphic, and the rhythm sags where the packaging row centres one label under three objects. Up close the text is weak: the sans captions are only about 3.5 mm tall, and mashing's '(mash)' is left alone on its own line. Garbled pseudo-letters ('E. 1E') sit on the kettle caps.
designs.fix: Add a strong title lockup (HOW BEER IS MADE) at the top as the anchor, and rebalance the captions to two even lines with nothing left alone on a line. Clean the garbled marks off the vessel caps.

designs.title: Gin Botanicals
designs.why: Good plate composition: five specimens staggered in a natural zigzag, with tight italic serif Latin names and a proper scientific-plate feel. Seen whole it is the most 'designed' of the three. At full size, though, the 'engraving' is a mottled, broken-dash threshold texture. It is not continuous hatching, so the berries and root surfaces look like noise and would print as splotchy ink. Juniper and angelica are visually much heavier than coriander and orris, so the weight is lopsided toward the left column. There is no title or rule to frame it as a plate.
designs.fix: Re-render the art as true line engraving (continuous, evenly spaced hatch lines, with tone made by line weight instead of speckle), then even out the tonal weight across the five specimens.

designs.title: Vineyard
designs.why: Nice vignette: the eye travels from the farmhouse and cypresses down the terraces to the vines in the foreground. The spaced-capital serif wordmark is elegant. But the line quality falls apart at full size into dotted, broken dashes, especially on the buildings and the path, so it looks like a traced photo, not an engraving. About a quarter of the height is empty sky above an off-centre house, which makes the top weak. The wordmark is small and loosely tied to the image, and the trailing period reads as a typo, not a stylistic choice.
designs.fix: Redraw as clean, continuous engraved line work, and tighten the crop so the farmhouse and cypresses anchor the top. Then enlarge the VINEYARD wordmark and set it closer to the image so they lock up as one unit.
